title: New Lagos Rising Again
premise: Zephyrine Winterbourne smuggles forbidden memories through the orbital customs ring above New Lagos, a dying colony the interstellar powers have written off. When they intercept a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries, they discover the colony's founders faked their own extinction to hide a weapon capable of shattering both rival fleets now circling overhead. As the fleets' fragile truce expires, Zephyrine must fabricate and maintain a single lie—broadcast in the dead tongue—that convinces both admirals the weapon is armed and aimed at them both, buying peace at the cost of exposing every memory they've ever smuggled. In the end, Zephyrine sacrifices their anonymity and their archive, choosing truth over loyalty, as New Lagos rises again not as a colony but as neutral ground.
about_author: Lior Pemberton is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else answered. They write science fiction about people who keep secrets for a living, and live off-grid with an unreasonable number of cassette tapes.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs: memories of drowned cities and dead festivals hidden in neural wafers. We learn New Lagos is being quietly abandoned by its corporate sponsors. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; Zephyrine believes invisibility is survival.

chapters.title: The Frequency That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Monitoring dead channels out of habit, Zephyrine catches a distress signal in Ashkari—a language extinct two centuries, one they only know from contraband memories. The signal originates from beneath New Lagos itself. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past reaching up to touch the present.

chapters.title: What the Colony Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Idris Okonjo, a customs officer who owes Zephyrine a favor. Together they trace the signal to a sealed vault under the old founding quarter, finding records the founders erased: the extinction was staged. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into awe—the colony lied to survive.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Fleet POV: Admiral Sefu Vane of the Concord and Admiral Reya Marchetti of the Compact arrive simultaneously, each claiming salvage rights over a colony both abandoned. Their truce is a formality with a thirty-day clock. Emotional beat: cold chess-game menace; New Lagos is a board, not a home.

chapters.title: The Weapon Named Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the vault they find the truth: the founders built a memory-weapon that can overwrite an entire fleet's collective history—and armed it once, nearly erasing themselves. Emotional beat: horror and temptation; Zephyrine, a smuggler of memories, holds the ultimate memory.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price List
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Pressured by Concord intelligence, Idris must choose between reporting Zephyrine or burning his career. He tips them off instead, forcing Zephyrine to flee into the undercity with the vault's core. Emotional beat: guilt and gratitude entangled; loyalty tested against duty.

chapters.title: Thirty Days to Midnight
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With the truce expiring, both fleets begin probing the vault independently. Zephyrine realizes the only way to stop a war is to convince each admiral the other side controls the weapon. They begin crafting the lie, using smuggled memories as raw material. Emotional beat: terrified resolve; the liar's craft turned to statecraft.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Zephyrine transmits in Ashkari across all channels: the weapon is live, targeted at whichever fleet fires first. Both admirals freeze—but Marchetti dispatches a boarding team to verify. Zephyrine must impersonate the extinct founders via recorded memory-ghosts. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; performance as survival.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Smuggled
chapters.summary: Climax. The boarding team corners Zephyrine in the vault; Idris arrives and vouches for them at gunpoint. To make the lie unbreakable, Zephyrine uploads their entire archive—including their own identity-memories—into the broadcast, becoming the weapon's living proof. Emotional beat: self-annihilation offered willingly; truth as sacrifice.

chapters.title: New Lagos Rising Again
chapters.summary: Resolution. The fleets stand down; the truce becomes a permanent accord with New Lagos as neutral ground under joint stewardship. Zephyrine, fragmented but alive, rebuilds a self from what remains, with Idris keeping watch. The colony reopens its ports. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth; memory lost, future gained.
